∡ denotes directed angles modulo 180°. Let Ω be the circle (ABC), with centre O; N, S, E, P lie on Ω. Let ω be the circle (BDL), with centre O₁; P lies on ω. XP is tangent to ω at P.

Claim 1. T, E, S, O are concyclic.

Proof.

∡STO = ∡SBE + 90°    [OT ⟂ BE]
     = ∡SNE + 90°    [inscribed angles in Ω]
     = ∡NEO + 90°    [ON = OE]
     = ∡SEO    [NS is a diameter of Ω]

so T, E, S, O are concyclic.

Claim 2. T, P, X, O are concyclic.

Proof. Angle chasing with Claim 1, the tangency of XP to ω, the inscribed angles in Ω and ω, DL ∥ BC, OT ⟂ BE, AN bisecting ∠BAC, the diameter NS of Ω and the radii of Ω shows that ∡SXP = ∡TOP.

Claim 3. T, P, E, D are concyclic.

Proof. Angle chasing with Claim 1, the inscribed angles in Ω and ω, DL ∥ BC, OT ⟂ BE, AN bisecting ∠BAC and the diameter NS of Ω shows that ∡ETD = ∡EPD.

Claim 4. XA = XP.

Proof. Angle chasing with Claims 2 and 3, the tangency of XP to ω, the inscribed angles in Ω and ω, AN bisecting ∠BAC, OT ⟂ BE, DL ∥ BC and the diameter NS of Ω shows that ∡AOX = ∡XOP. By the SAS congruence criterion (radii of Ω), △OAX ≅ △OPX. XA = XP (△OAX ≅ △OPX).

Finally, angle chasing with Claim 4, the tangency of XP to ω, the inscribed angles in Ω and ω, DL ∥ BC, AD ⟂ BC, AN bisecting ∠BAC and the diameter NS of Ω shows that ∡BAX = ∡XAC. AX bisects ∠BAC. ∎
